subproblems.title: Locality and uniqueness of the weight measure of integer multiplicity currents (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.16)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U₁, U₂, W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with W ⊆ U₁ and W ⊆ U₂, let T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U₁) and T₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(U₂) (GeometricCurrentOn) and let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) ∈ IMRep U₁ n and R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) ∈ IMRep U₂ n be integer multiplicity representations with R₁.Represents T₁ and R₂.Represents T₂. Suppose that T₁ and T₂ agree on W, i.e. currentEval T₁ ω = currentEval T₂ ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(W) (TestFormOn W n: a smooth compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Then the weight measures μ_i := R_i.measure = θ_i·Hⁿ⌞M_i (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) agree on W: μ₁.restrict W = μ₂.restrict W, i.e. μ₁(B ∩ W) = μ₂(B ∩ W) for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U₁ U₂ W : Set (Euclid P)) (T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U₁ n) (T₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U₂ n) (R₁ : IMRep U₁ n) (R₂ : IMRep U₂ n), IsOpen U₁ → IsOpen U₂ → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U₁ → W ⊆ U₂ → R₁.Represents T₁ → R₂.Represents T₂ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn W n, currentEval T₁ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = currentEval T₂ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) → R₁.measure.restrict W = R₂.measure.restrict W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0.5 of the parent proof (its first assertion and consequence (ii)); Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 768–772: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and 2.16 (lines 335–337, equality of currents in an open set). Inherited dependency (a resolved dependency of the parent node): dtc_mass_eq_measure (M): if U is open, W' ⊆ U is open and R represents T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), then T.massOn W' = R.measure W'. No sibling is used.
Notation. For an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ), R.measure = (Hⁿ.restrict M).withDensity θ, so R.measure(B) = ∫⁻_{B∩M} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. Put μ_i := R_i.measure (i = 1, 2).
1. (Masses of T₁ and T₂ agree on every open V ⊆ W.) Let V ⊆ W be open. By definition T_i.massOn V is the supremum of ofReal(T_i(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U_i n V, i.e. over test forms ω in U_i with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y (Euclidean coefficient norm). A differential form ω with IsTestForm ω and tsupport ω ⊆ V belongs to TestFormOn U₁ n, to TestFormOn U₂ n and to TestFormOn W n, because V ⊆ W ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂; hence the two admissible families consist of the same underlying forms. For such ω, T_i(ω) = currentEval T_i ω (definition of currentEval: the condition IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U_i holds), and the hypothesis, applied to ω regarded as an element of TestFormOn W n, gives currentEval T₁ ω = currentEval T₂ ω. So the two sets {ofReal(T_i(ω))} coincide and T₁.massOn V = T₂.massOn V. By M (applied in U_i, which is open, to the open set V ⊆ U_i), μ₁(V) = T₁.massOn V = T₂.massOn V = μ₂(V).
2. (Finiteness on relatively compact open subsets of W.) If V is open and closure V is a compact subset of W, then μ_i(V) ≤ μ_i(closure V) = ∫⁻_{M_i ∩ closure V} θ_i dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R_i, since closure V is a compact subset of W ⊆ U_i.
3. (Exhaustion of W.) For q ∈ ℕ, q ≥ 1, let V_q := ball(0, q) ∖ cthickening(1/q, ℝ^P ∖ W) (so V_q = ball(0, q) if W = ℝ^P). V_q is open (an open set minus a closed set) and V_q ⊆ V_{q+1}. Its closure is contained in closedBall(0, q) ∖ thickening(1/q, ℝ^P ∖ W), a compact set contained in W (a point whose distance to ℝ^P ∖ W is at least 1/q does not lie in ℝ^P ∖ W). Finally ⋃_q V_q = W: if y ∈ W choose r > 0 with ball(y, r) ⊆ W; then dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ r, and y ∈ V_q as soon as q > |y| and 1/q < r.
4. (Equality on each V_q.) Fix q and let ν_i := μ_i.restrict V_q. By step 2 each ν_i is a finite measure. For every open O ⊆ ℝ^P, ν_i(O) = μ_i(O ∩ V_q) and O ∩ V_q is an open subset of W, so ν₁(O) = ν₂(O) by step 1; in particular ν₁(ℝ^P) = ν₂(ℝ^P). The Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P is generated by the open sets, which form a π-system (Mathlib isPiSystem_isOpen), and two finite measures that agree on a generating π-system and on the whole space are equal (Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite). Hence ν₁ = ν₂.
5. (Conclusion.) Let B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Since the open sets V_q increase to W, continuity from below gives μ_i(B ∩ W) = lim_q μ_i(B ∩ V_q) = lim_q ν_i(B), and these limits coincide by step 4. Therefore (μ₁.restrict W)(B) = μ₁(B ∩ W) = μ₂(B ∩ W) = (μ₂.restrict W)(B) for every measurable B, i.e. μ₁.restrict W = μ₂.restrict W. ∎
Remark (how the siblings use this). With U₁ = U₂ = W = U and T₁ = T₂ = T one gets R₁.measure.restrict U = R₂.measure.restrict U for two representations of the same T ∈ 𝒟_n(U); since the carriers lie in U, R_i.measure.restrict U = R_i.measure (Mathlib restrict_withDensity and Measure.restrict_restrict), so the weight μ_T := R.measure does not depend on the representation (Simon 6.3.2(3)). This consequence was checked in Lean from the exact type above.
proof_key_steps: For open V ⊆ W the admissible forms for M_V(T₁) and M_V(T₂) are the same forms and T₁, T₂ agree on them, so M_V(T₁) = M_V(T₂); by dtc_mass_eq_measure μ₁(V) = μ₂(V).
μ_i(V) < ∞ whenever closure V is a compact subset of W (local integrability of θ_i).
Exhaust W by open V_q ↑ W with compact closures in W; the finite measures μ_i⌞V_q agree on the open-set π-system and on ℝ^P, hence are equal.
Continuity from below along V_q ↑ W gives μ₁.restrict W = μ₂.restrict W.

subproblems.title: Convergence of integrals from limsup on compact sets and liminf on bounded open sets
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)). Assume (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K; (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every bounded open G ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup and lim inf taken in [0, ∞]). Then for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support, ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ (Bochner integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → Bornology.IsBounded G → μ G ≤ liminf (fun j => μs j G) atTop) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, f x ∂(μs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6.3 of the parent proof, i.e. the 'standard approximation argument' that ends Simon's proof of 7.2.4 (chapter-07.txt lines 285–288). No dependencies; Mathlib's layer-cake formulas and Fatou lemmas.
Let f be continuous with compact support, K₀ := tsupport f (compact) and M₀ := sup_y |f(y)| < ∞. If M₀ = 0 then f = 0 and all integrals vanish, so assume M₀ > 0.
1. (Eventual finiteness.) By (a), μ(K₀) < ∞. By (b), limsup_j μ_j(K₀) ≤ μ(K₀) < μ(K₀) + 1, so there is j₁ with μ_j(K₀) ≤ A := μ(K₀) + 1 < ∞ for all j ≥ j₁. For ν ∈ {μ} ∪ {μ_j : j ≥ j₁}, f is ν-integrable: it is continuous, hence Borel, |f| ≤ M₀·1_{K₀} and ν(K₀) < ∞.
2. (Reduction to nonnegative functions.) Write f = f⁺ − f⁻ with f^± := max(±f, 0). These are continuous, nonnegative, vanish outside K₀ and are bounded by M₀, and ∫ f dν = ∫ f⁺ dν − ∫ f⁻ dν for the measures ν of step 1. Finitely many indices do not affect limits, so it suffices to show ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ for every continuous g ≥ 0 vanishing outside K₀ with g ≤ M₀.
3. (Layer cake.) Fix such a g. For every Borel measure ν on ℝ^P (Mathlib MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt and MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le; g ≥ 0 is measurable):
   ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dν = ∫⁻_{t∈(0,∞)} ν({g > t}) dt = ∫⁻_{t∈(0,∞)} ν({g ≥ t}) dt.
For t ≥ M₀ the set {g > t} is empty and for t > M₀ the set {g ≥ t} is empty. For t > 0, {g > t} is open (g continuous) and contained in K₀, hence bounded; {g ≥ t} is closed and contained in K₀, hence compact. The functions t ↦ ν({g > t}) and t ↦ ν({g ≥ t}) are antitone, hence measurable.
4. (Lower bound.) By (c), μ({g > t}) ≤ liminf_j μ_j({g > t}) for every t > 0. Put F_j(t) := μ_j({g > t}). By step 3 and Fatou's lemma for lower integrals (Mathlib MeasureTheory.lintegral_liminf_le, on (0, ∞) with Lebesgue measure): ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ({g > t}) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} liminf_j F_j dt ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} F_j dt = liminf_j ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j.
5. (Upper bound.) Put G_j(t) := μ_j({g ≥ t}). For j ≥ j₁ and t > 0, G_j(t) ≤ μ_j(K₀)·1_{(0,M₀]}(t) ≤ A·1_{(0,M₀]}(t), and ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} A·1_{(0,M₀]} dt = A·M₀ < ∞. By the reverse Fatou lemma (Mathlib MeasureTheory.limsup_lintegral_le, applied to the shifted sequence (G_{j₁+i})_i, which has the same lim sup) and by (b) for the compact sets {g ≥ t}, t > 0: limsup_j ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j = limsup_j ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} G_j dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} limsup_j G_j dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ({g ≥ t}) dt = ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ.
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 4 and 5 give ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j → ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ in [0, ∞]; the limit is ≤ M₀μ(K₀) < ∞ and the terms are ≤ M₀A < ∞ for j ≥ j₁. For a nonnegative integrable g, ∫ g dν = (∫⁻ ofReal(g) dν).toReal (Mathlib integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae), and toReal is continuous at finite values, so ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ. By step 2, ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: By (a) and (b), μ_j(tsupport f) is eventually bounded, so f is eventually μ_j-integrable; split f = f⁺ − f⁻.
Layer cake: ∫ g dν = ∫_0^∞ ν({g > t}) dt = ∫_0^∞ ν({g ≥ t}) dt, with {g > t} bounded open and {g ≥ t} compact for t > 0.
Fatou with (c) gives the liminf inequality; reverse Fatou with the eventual bound and (b) gives the limsup inequality.
Convert lintegrals back to Bochner integrals and recombine f⁺ and f⁻.

subproblems.title: Local C¹ retraction onto an embedded C² submanifold with Lipschitz constant tending to 1
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be a d-dimensional embedded C² submanifold in the sense of the contract (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N: every y ∈ N has an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W and a map ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P which is C² on V and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(v) injective for every v ∈ V), and let x ∈ N. Then there are δ > 0 and a map π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that (i) π is C¹ on the open ball B_δ(x); (ii) π(B_δ(x)) ⊆ N; (iii) π(y) = y for every y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x); (iv) for every η > 0 there is s with 0 < s ≤ δ and |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → x ∈ N → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (π : Euclid P → Euclid P), 0 < δ ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 π (ball x δ) ∧ MapsTo π (ball x δ) N ∧ (∀ y ∈ N ∩ ball x δ, π y = y) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s ≤ δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ ball x s, ∀ z ∈ ball x s, ‖π y - π z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3.1 of the parent proof, which takes for π the nearest-point projection onto N given by the tubular neighbourhood theorem (cf. Simon 7.5, chapter-07.txt lines 783–786). The parent uses only properties (i)–(iv) of that projection. Here they are proved for the explicit graph retraction over T_xN, which agrees with the nearest-point projection to first order at x; this avoids the tubular neighbourhood theorem and is the only departure from the parent's text. No dependencies; Mathlib's inverse function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, ContDiffAt.localInverse) and mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le).
1. (Chart at x.) Apply IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N at y := x to get V, W, ψ as in the statement. Since x ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = x. As V is open and ψ is C² on V, ψ is differentiable on V with continuous derivative. L := Dψ(v₀) : ℝ^d → ℝ^P is an injective linear map; Q := L(ℝ^d) is a subspace and L : ℝ^d → Q is a linear isomorphism with inverse L⁻¹ : Q → ℝ^d. Let p : ℝ^P → Q be the orthogonal projection (‖p‖ ≤ 1 and p(Lw) = Lw) and A := L⁻¹∘p : ℝ^P → ℝ^d (continuous linear).
2. (Local inverse.) h : ℝ^d → ℝ^d, h(v) := A(ψ(v) − x), is C² near v₀, h(v₀) = 0 and Dh(v₀) = A∘L = id. By the inverse function theorem there are open sets V₀ ⊆ V with v₀ ∈ V₀ and O ⊆ ℝ^d with 0 ∈ O such that h maps V₀ bijectively onto O and the inverse k : O → V₀ is C¹; so k(h(v)) = v for v ∈ V₀ and h(k(u)) = u for u ∈ O.
3. (Graph parametrization.) Φ := ψ∘k : O → ℝ^P is C¹, Φ(0) = ψ(v₀) = x, Φ(O) = ψ(V₀) ⊆ N, and DΦ(0) = Dψ(v₀)∘Dk(0) = L∘(Dh(v₀))⁻¹ = L.
4. (ψ(V₀) is relatively open in N.) Let F := V ∖ V₀, a relatively closed subset of V. Then ψ(F) is relatively closed in W: if y ∈ W and y = lim ψ(f_i) with f_i ∈ F, then K := {y} ∪ {ψ(f_i) : i ∈ ℕ} is a compact subset of W, so all f_i lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K); a subsequence converges to some f ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K), f ∈ F because F is closed in V, and ψ(f) = y by continuity of ψ at f. Hence W₀ := W ∖ ψ(F) is open. x ∈ W₀, because x = ψ(v₀) with v₀ ∉ F and ψ is injective on V. Moreover W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V₀): if y ∈ W₀ ∩ N then y ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), so y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V, and v ∉ F (otherwise y ∈ ψ(F)), i.e. v ∈ V₀; conversely ψ(V₀) ⊆ W ∩ N and ψ(V₀) ∩ ψ(F) = ∅ by injectivity.
5. (Choice of δ and π.) Choose r₀ > 0 with B^d_{r₀}(0) ⊆ O and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ W₀ and ‖A‖δ < r₀. Define π(y) := Φ(A(y − x)) for y ∈ B_δ(x) and π(y) := y otherwise. For y ∈ B_δ(x), |A(y − x)| ≤ ‖A‖|y − x| < r₀, so A(y − x) ∈ O.
6. ((i)–(iii).) (i) On the open ball B_δ(x), π is the composition of the affine map y ↦ A(y − x) (with values in O) and the C¹ map Φ, hence C¹. (ii) π(y) ∈ Φ(O) ⊆ N for y ∈ B_δ(x). (iii) If y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ N ∩ W₀ = ψ(V₀), write y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V₀; then A(y − x) = h(v) ∈ O and π(y) = ψ(k(h(v))) = ψ(v) = y. In particular π(x) = x.
7. ((iv).) For y ∈ B_δ(x), Dπ(y) = DΦ(A(y − x))∘A; hence Dπ(x) = L∘L⁻¹∘p = p and ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1. Dπ is continuous on B_δ(x) because π is C¹ there. Given η > 0 choose s ∈ (0, δ] with ‖Dπ(y) − Dπ(x)‖ ≤ η, hence ‖Dπ(y)‖ ≤ 1 + η, for all y ∈ B_s(x). B_s(x) is convex and π is differentiable on it, so the mean value inequality gives |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x). ∎
(The case d = 0 is included: then ℝ^d is a point, L = 0 is injective, Q = {0}, p = 0, A = 0, Φ ≡ x and π ≡ x on B_δ(x), and B_δ(x) ∩ N = {x} by step 4.)
proof_key_steps: Take a chart ψ at x, L := Dψ(v₀), Q := range L, p the orthogonal projection onto Q and A := L⁻¹p.
Inverse function theorem for h := A(ψ − x) at v₀ gives the C¹ graph parametrization Φ := ψ∘h⁻¹ of N near x with DΦ(0) = L.
Properness of the chart makes ψ(V₀) relatively open in N, so N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(V₀) for small δ.
π(y) := Φ(A(y − x)) is C¹, maps into N, fixes N ∩ B_δ(x), and Dπ(x) = p has norm ≤ 1; continuity of Dπ and the mean value inequality give Lipschitz constants 1 + η on small balls.

Source: steps 0.1–0.4, 0.6 and 3.2 of the parent proof (Simon 7.3.1, proof display (1), chapter-07.txt lines 329–337). Sibling used: local_retraction (RET). Inherited dependencies (resolved dependencies of the parent node): dtc_blowUp_scaling (BU) and dtc_vanish_off_support (V). SimonGMT facts: GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, restrictDomain_apply, boundary_affinePushforward and tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset (Chapter06/AffineCurrentPushforward.lean, CurrentLocalEquality.lean), zeroRegion and support (CurrentLocalEquality.lean). The hypotheses ℓ ≤ k and (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ of the parent are not needed here (local closedness of N near x is built into the proper charts used by RET), so they are not assumed.
Notation: n := m + 1, P := n + k, λ_j := lams j, η_j := dilation x λ_j, so η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x) and η_j⁻¹(z) = x + λ_jz. 'For all large j' means 'for all j ≥ some j₀'.
0. (Unfolding the blow-up.) η_j is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with η_j(ball(x, s)) = ball(0, s/λ_j), η_j(closedBall(x, s)) = closedBall(0, s/λ_j), η_j⁻¹(U_j) = U and η_j(A ∩ B) = η_j(A) ∩ η_j(B). By the definitions of blowUp, affinePushforward_apply and restrictDomain_apply, S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) for every test form ω in U_j, where η_j^#ω := affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P λ_j) (−λ_j⁻¹x) ω is a test form in U with tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset). Since the boundary commutes with affinePushforward (boundary_affinePushforward) and with restrictDomain (both are composition with d on test forms), ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j), again with tsupport(η_j^#β) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport β).
1. ((1)) U_j is the image of the open set U under the homeomorphism η_j, hence open.
2. (A good radius.) x ∈ spt T ⊆ U ∩ N, so x ∈ U and x ∈ N. Since n = m + 1, boundarySupport T = spt ∂T = U ∖ Z_∂ with Z_∂ := zeroRegion(∂T) open; x ∈ U and x ∉ spt ∂T give x ∈ Z_∂. Choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ U ∩ Z_∂.
3. ((2)) Let R ∈ ℝ. If R < 0, closedBall(0, R) = ∅. If R ≥ 0, then for every j with λ_jR ≤ 2r (all large j, as λ_j → 0), closedBall(0, R) ⊆ η_j(closedBall(x, λ_jR)) ⊆ η_j(U), because z = η_j(x + λ_jz).
4. ((3)) BU(3), applied with A := U ∩ N (U is open and n > 0) to IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N), gives IsMinimizingIn S_j (η_j(U ∩ N)) for every j.
5. ((4)) Let Z_T := zeroRegion(T), an open set with spt T = U ∖ Z_T. Let z ∈ U_j ∖ η_j(spt T). Then η_j⁻¹(z) ∈ U ∖ spt T = Z_T, so z ∈ η_j(Z_T), an open subset of U_j. Choose ε > 0 with closedBall(z, ε) ⊆ η_j(Z_T) and put W' := ball(z, ε/2): W' is open and its closure closedBall(z, ε/2) is compact and contained in U_j. If ω is a test form in U_j with tsupport ω ⊆ W', then tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(closedBall(z, ε/2)) ⊆ Z_T is disjoint from spt T, so S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) = 0 by V. Thus S_j vanishes on W', W' ⊆ zeroRegion(S_j) and z ∉ spt S_j. Hence spt S_j ⊆ η_j(spt T) ⊆ η_j(U ∩ N) = A_j.
6. ((5)) Let R ∈ ℝ. If R ≤ 0 then ball(0, R) = ∅; a form with tsupport ⊆ ∅ is 0, so the only admissible form for massOn ∅ is ω = 0 and S_j.massOn ∅ = ofReal(S_j(0)) = 0; take c := 0. Let R > 0. HasMassDensity T x θ gives θ ≥ 0 and F(s) := T.massOn(ball(x, s)) / (ω_n·ofReal(sⁿ)) → ofReal θ as s → 0⁺, where ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞) is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝⁿ. Since ofReal θ < ofReal(θ + 1), there is s₀ > 0 with F(s) < ofReal(θ + 1) for 0 < s < s₀; as ω_n·ofReal(sⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞) this gives T.massOn(ball(x, s)) ≤ ofReal(θ + 1)·ω_n·ofReal(sⁿ). For j with λ_jR < s₀ (all large j), BU(1) with W := ball(x, λ_jR), together with η_j(ball(x, λ_jR)) = ball(0, R), gives S_j.massOn(ball(0, R)) = ofReal(λ_j⁻ⁿ)·T.massOn(ball(x, λ_jR)) ≤ ofReal(λ_j⁻ⁿ)·ofReal(θ + 1)·ω_n·ofReal(λ_jⁿRⁿ) = ofReal(θ + 1)·ω_n·ofReal(Rⁿ) =: c < ∞.
7. ((6)) Let R ∈ ℝ and let j satisfy λ_jR < 2r (all large j; every j if R ≤ 0). If β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j) and tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, R), then by step 0 ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) and tsupport(η_j^#β) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(ball(0, R)) = ball(x, λ_jR) ⊆ ball(x, 2r) ⊆ Z_∂, which is disjoint from spt ∂T; so ∂T(η_j^#β) = 0 by V applied to ∂T.
8. ((7)) Apply RET to N (dimension d := n + ℓ) and x ∈ N: δ > 0 and π with RET(i)–(iv); π(x) = x by RET(iii). Let s₁ ∈ (0, δ] be given by RET(iv) for η = 1 (π is 2-Lipschitz on B_{s₁}(x)), and for η > 0 let s(η) ∈ (0, δ] be given by RET(iv). Let G > 0 and define π_j(z) := η_j(π(x + λ_jz)) = λ_j⁻¹(π(x + λ_jz) − x). Let j satisfy λ_jG < min(s₁, r) (all large j). Then:
 (a) z ↦ x + λ_jz maps ball(0, G) into ball(x, λ_jG) ⊆ B_δ(x), so π_j is C¹ on ball(0, G) (composition of affine maps with π, which is C¹ on B_δ(x)).
 (b) For z ∈ ball(0, G) put y := x + λ_jz ∈ B_{s₁}(x). Then π(y) ∈ N by RET(ii), and |π(y) − x| = |π(y) − π(x)| ≤ 2|y − x| = 2λ_j|z| < 2r, so π(y) ∈ ball(x, 2r) ⊆ U. Hence π(y) ∈ U ∩ N and π_j(z) = η_j(π(y)) ∈ A_j; moreover |π_j(z)| = λ_j⁻¹|π(y) − x| ≤ 2|z|.
 (c) If z ∈ A_j ∩ ball(0, G), then y' := x + λ_jz ∈ U ∩ N (z ∈ η_j(U ∩ N) and η_j is injective) and y' ∈ B_δ(x), so π(y') = y' by RET(iii) and π_j(z) = η_j(y') = z.
 (d) Given η > 0, for j with λ_jG < s(η) (all large j) and y, z ∈ ball(0, G), the points x + λ_jy and x + λ_jz lie in B_{s(η)}(x), so |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| = λ_j⁻¹|π(x + λ_jy) − π(x + λ_jz)| ≤ λ_j⁻¹(1 + η)λ_j|y − z| = (1 + η)|y − z|.
This proves (7) with πs := (π_j)_j, and the proof is complete. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold blowUp: S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) and ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) with tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport ω).
Choose r with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ U ∩ zeroRegion(∂T); then U_j ⊇ closedBall(0, R) and ∂S_j = 0 on B_R(0) once λ_jR < 2r.
Minimality and mass scaling come from dtc_blowUp_scaling; HasMassDensity bounds M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) by (θ+1)ω_nRⁿ eventually; the support inclusion uses vanish_off_support.

subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity T), x ∈ U with x ∉ spt ∂T (x ∉ boundarySupport T), and λ_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ) with λ_j → 0. Then there is C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) such that the blow-ups S_j := η_{x,λ_j#}T (blowUp T x λ_j) satisfy S_j ⇀ C in ℝⁿ (ConvergesWeakly), μ_{S_j} → μ_C for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge), C is minimizing in ℝⁿ (IsMinimizingIn C univ; in particular C is integer multiplicity) and ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C). (In fact C = c[[ℝⁿ]] for some c ∈ ℤ.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the case k = 0, where ℝ^{n+k} = ℝⁿ), based on the Constancy Theorem, Simon Ch. 6, 2.34 (chapter-06.txt lines 571–600). Its analytic core is in the pinned library: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero (Chapter08/DistributionalConstancy.lean; standard axioms only): if f ∈ L¹_loc(V) on an open preconnected V ⊆ ℝⁿ and ∫ f·∂_iφ = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported φ with tsupport φ ⊆ V and every i, then f is a.e. constant on V. Sibling used: measure_locality (MEAS). Inherited dependencies: dtc_vanish_off_support (V), dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub (G).
Notation. n = m + 1. e₁, …, eₙ is the standard basis; for an n-covector α put α(e) := α(e₁, …, eₙ). Every alternating n-form α on ℝⁿ satisfies α(v₁, …, vₙ) = det[v₁ … vₙ]·α(e) (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). e* denotes the n-covector v ↦ det[v₁ … vₙ] (e*(e) = 1), and Hⁿ = μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). η_j := dilation x λ_j, U_j := η_j(U), S_j := blowUp T x λ_j.
1. (Lemma A: density of a top-dimensional IM current.) Let V ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and X ∈ 𝒟_n(V) be represented by R = (M, θ, ξ). For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M there are Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q, so dim Q = n and Q = ℝⁿ, and an orthonormal τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) spanning Q with ξ(y)(α) = ±α(τ) for all α; since α(τ) = det[τ]·α(e) and det[τ] = ±1 (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real), ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)·α(e) with σ(y) := ξ(y)(e*) ∈ {−1, 1}. The function σ is a.e.-strongly measurable on M (as ξ is). Put g := θσ on M and g := 0 off M (redefined on an Hⁿ-null set so that it is Borel and ℤ-valued). Then |g| ≤ θ·1_M, so g ∈ L¹_loc(V) by locallyIntegrable_mult, and X(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫ g(y) ω(y)(e) dy for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V).
2. (Lemma B: cycles have constant density.) In the situation of Lemma A let B ⊆ V be open, connected and nonempty, and assume X(dβ) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(V) with tsupport β ⊆ B. Then g = c a.e. on B for some c ∈ ℤ. Proof. For a ∈ C_c^∞ with tsupport a ⊆ B and i ∈ {1, …, n}, let β_i := a·γ_i, where γ_i is the constant (n−1)-covector with γ_i(e₁, …, ê_k, …, eₙ) = δ_{ik} (the coordinate form dx¹∧…∧dx^{i−1}∧dx^{i+1}∧…∧dxⁿ). Then dβ_i(y)(e) = (−1)^{i−1}∂_ia(y), so 0 = X(dβ_i) = (−1)^{i−1}∫ g ∂_ia. Now let φ be C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ B; let K := tsupport φ and choose δ₀ > 0 with cthickening(2δ₀, K) ⊆ B. For 0 < ε < δ₀ the mollification φ_ε := φ ∗ ρ_ε (ρ_ε a smooth mollifier supported in closedBall(0, ε)) is smooth with tsupport in K' := cthickening(δ₀, K) ⊆ B (compact), and ∂_iφ_ε = (∂_iφ) ∗ ρ_ε → ∂_iφ uniformly as ε → 0. As g ∈ L¹(K'), ∫ g ∂_iφ = lim_ε ∫ g ∂_iφ_ε = 0; here ∂_iφ(y) = Dφ(y)e_i. The library theorem ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero (B open and preconnected, g locally integrable on B) gives c ∈ ℝ with g = c a.e. on B. Since g is ℤ-valued and B has positive Lebesgue measure, c ∈ ℤ.
3. (T is constant near x.) Since n = m + 1, spt ∂T = U ∖ Z_∂ with Z_∂ := zeroRegion(∂T) open; x ∈ U ∖ spt ∂T gives x ∈ Z_∂. Choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ U ∩ Z_∂ and let B := ball(x, 2r) (open, connected). Let R represent T and let g be as in Lemma A (V := U). If β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and tsupport β ⊆ B, then tsupport β is disjoint from spt ∂T, so T(dβ) = ∂T(β) = 0 by V. Lemma B gives c ∈ ℤ with g = c a.e. on B.
4. (The limit C.) Define C(ω) := c∫ ω(y)(e) dy for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ). C is linear and sequentially continuous (if ω_q → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ) with supports in a compact K then |C(ω_q)| ≤ |c|·Lⁿ(K)·sup|ω_q| → 0), so C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ). C is integer multiplicity: if c = 0, C = 0 is represented by the IMRep with empty carrier; if c ≠ 0, by R_C := (carrier ℝⁿ, mult |c|, orient sign(c)·ε) with ε(α) := α(e₁, …, eₙ): ℝⁿ is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (it is the range of the 1-Lipschitz identity; Chapter03 countablyRectifiable_range), mult is constant ≥ 1 with ∫_K |c| dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K, the orientation is constant, and at every y the approximate tangent space of ℝⁿ is ℝⁿ = span(e₁, …, eₙ) (Chapter03 hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule with P = ⊤), oriented by ±ε (IsUnitOrientationOf with τ = e). Its action is ∫ |c|·sign(c)·ω(y)(e) dHⁿ = C(ω).
5. (The blow-ups agree with C on growing balls.) Let B'_j := η_j(B) = ball(0, 2r/λ_j) ⊆ U_j. For a test form ω in U_j with tsupport ω ⊆ B'_j: by the definition of blowUp (affine push-forward of the restriction), S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) with η_j^#ω(y) = ω(η_jy)∘(λ_j⁻¹I), so η_j^#ω(y)(e) = λ_j^{−n}ω(η_jy)(e), and tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ B. By Lemma A and step 3, S_j(ω) = ∫ g(y)λ_j^{−n}ω(η_jy)(e) dy = c∫ λ_j^{−n}ω(η_jy)(e) dy = c∫ ω(z)(e) dz = C(ω) (change of variables y = x + λ_jz, dy = λ_jⁿdz). Hence (*) currentEval(S_j, ω) = C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ) with tsupport ω ⊆ B'_j.
6. (ConvergesWeakly.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ); its tsupport is compact, hence contained in some ball(0, ρ). Since 2r/λ_j → ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ B'_j for all large j, and then currentEval(S_j, ω) = C(ω) by (*). So currentEval(S_j, ω) is eventually equal to C(ω).
7. (BoundaryVanishes C.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝⁿ), tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, ρ). For large j, tsupport dβ ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ B'_j, so C.boundary(β) = C(dβ) = S_j(dβ) by (*). As in step 5 (boundary_affinePushforward), S_j(dβ) = ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) with tsupport(η_j^#β) ⊆ B ⊆ Z_∂, so it vanishes by V. Hence C.boundary = 0.
8. (MassMeasuresConverge.) Let R_j represent S_j (in U_j), R represent C (in ℝⁿ), and f be continuous with compact support, tsupport f ⊆ ball(0, ρ). For j with ρ < 2r/λ_j, S_j and C agree on B'_j by (*), so MEAS (U₁ := U_j, U₂ := ℝⁿ, W := B'_j) gives R_j.measure.restrict B'_j = R.measure.restrict B'_j. As f = 0 off B'_j, ∫ f dR_j.measure = ∫ f d(R_j.measure.restrict B'_j) = ∫ f d(R.measure.restrict B'_j) = ∫ f dR.measure (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). The sequence is eventually constant, hence converges.

0. (Facts.) For an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V), V open, with representation R_Y and weight μ_Y := R_Y.measure: (F1) M_O(Y) = M_{O ∩ V}(Y) for every open O (the admissible forms coincide, since test forms in V have tsupport in V), and M_{O∩V}(Y) = μ_Y(O ∩ V) = μ_Y(O) by M (the carrier lies in V); (F2) μ_Y(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ V (locallyIntegrable_mult); (F3, locality of approximate tangent spaces) if O ⊆ ℝ^P is open and y ∈ O, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (A ∩ O) y Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A y Q for every A: for f ∈ C_c with tsupport f ⊆ ball(0, L), the sets η_{y,r}(A) and η_{y,r}(A ∩ O) agree inside ball(0, L) as soon as rL < dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ O), so the blow-up integrals coincide for small r. Consequently, for open O ⊆ V, (M_Y ∩ O, θ_Y, ξ_Y) is an IMRep in V (and in any open set containing its carrier and in which it is locally integrable), representing the current Y⌞O; for O open, Y⌞O agrees with Y on forms supported in O.
1. (Good radii.) For every integer R ≥ 1, by (i) and (iii) there is J(R) such that for all j ≥ J(R): closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j and ∂S_j vanishes on all β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j) with tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, R). Replacing J(R) by max_{R' ≤ R} J(R') we may assume J nondecreasing (the properties for R imply those for R' ≤ R). Put j₀ := J(8) and, for j ≥ j₀, R_j := max{R ∈ ℕ : 8 ≤ R ≤ max(8, j), J(R) ≤ j}. Then R_j ≥ 8, J(R_j) ≤ j, hence closedBall(0, R_j) ⊆ U_j and ∂S_j vanishes on ball(0, R_j); and R_j → ∞ (for R ≥ 8 and j ≥ max(R, J(R)), R_j ≥ R). Only indices j ≥ j₀ are used below.
2. (A good slicing radius.) Fix j ≥ j₀, let (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) represent S_j, μ_j := its weight, V := ball(0, R_j) and let S ∈ 𝒟_n(V) be S_j restricted to V (restrictDomain), represented by (M_j ∩ V, θ_j, ξ_j) (F3). Then ∂S = 0 and M_O(S) ≤ μ_j(closure O) < ∞ for O ⊂⊂ V (F1, F2). For 0 < t < R_j let S⌞B_t ∈ 𝒟_n(V) be the current represented by (M_j ∩ ball(0, t), θ_j, ξ_j); this is Simon's restriction T⌞{f < t} (2.7–2.9: μ_S = θ_jHⁿ⌞(M_j ∩ V) and S⃗ = ξ_j) for the 1-Lipschitz function f(y) := |y|, so ⟨S, f, t−⟩ = ∂(S⌞B_t) since ∂S = 0. By 4.10 with W := ball(0, 3R_j/4) ⊂⊂ V and (a, b) := (R_j/4, R_j/2): ∫_{R_j/4}^{R_j/2} M_W(∂(S⌞B_t)) dt ≤ M(S⌞{R_j/4 < |y| < R_j/2}) ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, R_j/2)) < ∞ (F2; closedBall(0, R_j/2) is a compact subset of U_j). Hence there is ρ'_j ∈ (R_j/4, R_j/2) with σ_j := M_W(∂(S⌞B_{ρ'_j})) < ∞.
3. (Truncation.) Let R̂_j := (M_j ∩ ball(0, ρ'_j), θ_j, ξ_j). It is an IMRep in ℝ^P: the carrier is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (a subset of M_j; CountablyRectifiable.mono), θ_j ≥ 1 on it, for compact K ∫_{carrier ∩ K} θ_j ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ'_j)) < ∞ (F2), ξ_j is measurable, and it orients the approximate tangent spaces a.e. by F3. The functional ω ↦ R̂_j.action(ω) is linear and sequentially continuous on 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (|R̂_j.action(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ'_j)), as |ξ_j(α)| ≤ |α| for a unit simple n-vector ξ_j), so it defines Ŝ_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), integer multiplicity, with R̂_j.Represents Ŝ_j.
 (a) (Agreement.) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, ρ'_j), then ω is a test form in U_j and Ŝ_j(ω) = ∫_{M_j ∩ ball} θ_jξ_j(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{M_j} θ_jξ_j(ω) dHⁿ = S_j(ω) = currentEval(S_j, ω), since ω = 0 off the ball.

The carrier of R̂_j lies in ball(0, ρ'_j), where χ = 1 and dχ = 0, so ∂Ŝ_j(β) = Ŝ_j(dβ) = Ŝ_j(χdβ) = Ŝ_j(d(χβ)) (d(χβ) = dχ∧β + χdβ). Now χβ ∈ 𝒟^m(V) with tsupport ⊆ W, and Ŝ_j(d(χβ)) = (S⌞B_{ρ'_j})(d(χβ)) = ∂(S⌞B_{ρ'_j})(χβ) (both are the action of the same triple). By the definition of M_W as a supremum (applied to ±χβ/sup|χβ|), |∂Ŝ_j(β)| ≤ σ_j·sup|χβ| ≤ σ_j·sup|β|. Hence M_O(∂Ŝ_j) ≤ σ_j for every O.

By (ii) there are c_R < ∞ and j₁ with M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ c_R for j ≥ j₁; take j₂ ≥ max(j₀, j₁) with ρ'_j > R for j ≥ j₂ (ρ'_j > R_j/4 → ∞). For j ≥ j₂, M_O(Ŝ_j) ≤ M_O(S_j) ≤ M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ c_R by 3(d) and monotonicity of massOn, and M_O(∂Ŝ_j) = 0 by 3(c). For j₀ ≤ j < j₂, M_O(Ŝ_j) ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ'_j)) < ∞ and M_O(∂Ŝ_j) ≤ σ_j < ∞. So sup_{j ≥ j₀}(M_O(Ŝ_j) + M_O(∂Ŝ_j)) < ∞.
5. (Federer–Fleming.) By step 4 the integer multiplicity currents (Ŝ_j)_{j ≥ j₀} in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfy the hypothesis of Simon 3.11 in U = ℝ^P (n ≥ 1, P − n ≥ 1; every W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P is bounded). Hence there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → {j : j ≥ j₀} and an integer multiplicity C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with Ŝ_{φ(i)} ⇀ C.
6. (Output.) Put Ŝ_i := Ŝ_{φ(i)} (re-indexed) and ρ_i := ρ'_{φ(i)}. Then φ is strictly increasing; C and all Ŝ_i are integer multiplicity; the bound of step 4 holds for the subsequence; Ŝ_i ⇀ C; ρ_i → ∞ (φ(i) → ∞ and ρ'_j > R_j/4 → ∞); closedBall(0, ρ_i) ⊆ ball(0, R_{φ(i)}) ⊆ U_{φ(i)}; and the agreement 3(a) holds. ∂C = 0: for β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, ρ), for all large i we have ρ < ρ_i and C.boundary(β) = C(dβ) = lim_i Ŝ_i(dβ) = lim_i ∂Ŝ_i(β) = 0 by 3(c). ConvergesWeakly: for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, ρ), for all large i, currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) = Ŝ_i(ω) by 3(a), and Ŝ_i(ω) → C(ω). ∎

Fix K, ε and ψ.
1. (Reduction to ψ = id.) Hypotheses (1)–(5) are preserved when (U_j, A_j, S_j, Ŝ_j, ρ_j) is replaced by (U_{ψ(j)}, A_{ψ(j)}, S_{ψ(j)}, Ŝ_{ψ(j)}, ρ_{ψ(j)}): statements for all large j and limits transfer along ψ(j) → ∞, a subsequence of a weakly convergent sequence converges weakly, and a supremum over a subsequence is smaller. A strictly increasing φ' that works for the re-indexed sequence gives the claim for S_{ψ(φ'(i))}. So assume ψ = id. If K = ∅ take W := ∅ and φ' := id: M_∅(·) = 0 (the only admissible form is 0). Assume K ≠ ∅.
2. (Cut-off; book (1).) Let ε₁ := min(ε, 1)/2 and choose ψ_c ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with ψ_c = 1 on a neighbourhood of K and tsupport ψ_c ⊆ thickening(ε₁, K) (compact). Put W_s := {ψ_c > s} for 0 ≤ s < 1 (open, K ⊆ W_s ⊆ thickening(ε, K)), Σ_s := {ψ_c = s} and F_s := {ψ_c ≥ s} (compact for s > 0), and L₀ := sup|Dψ_c| (a Lipschitz constant of ψ_c). Fix G ≥ 1 with tsupport ψ_c ⊆ ball(0, G/3) and write B_G := ball(0, G).
3. (Good indices.) Apply hypothesis (3) with radius 2G to get maps π_j. There is j₀ such that for j ≥ j₀: (R1) π_j is C¹ on ball(0, 2G), maps it into A_j, fixes A_j ∩ ball(0, 2G) and satisfies |π_j(y)| ≤ 2|y| there; (R2) ρ_j > G, so closedBall(0, G) ⊆ ball(0, ρ_j) ⊆ U_j; (R3) M_{B_G}(S_j) ≤ c_G (hypothesis (2) with R = G). For η > 0 let j(η) ≥ j₀ be such that π_j is (1 + η)-Lipschitz on ball(0, 2G) for j ≥ j(η); then ‖Dπ_j(y)‖ ≤ 1 + η for y ∈ ball(0, 2G).
4. (Flat convergence; book (2).) M_W(∂C) ≤ liminf_j M_W(∂Ŝ_j) < ∞ for bounded open W (lower semicontinuity of mass, SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf applied to ∂Ŝ_j ⇀ ∂C), so C and the Ŝ_j belong to Simon's class I in U = ℝ^P, and by 7.2, d_{W₀}(Ŝ_j, C) → 0 for W₀ := {ψ_c > 0} (bounded open). By the definition 7.1 of d_{W₀} (take decompositions within 1/j of the infimum and change signs) there are IM R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (n + 1 ≤ P) and IM S'_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with C − Ŝ_j = ∂R_j + S'_j and a_j := M_{W₀}(R_j) + M_{W₀}(S'_j) → 0. ∂R_j = C − Ŝ_j − S'_j is IM (F4) and has locally finite mass (F1).
5. (Slicing and choice of α; book (3)–(5).) Choose φ₁ strictly increasing with φ₁(i) ≥ j₀ and Σ_i a_{φ₁(i)} < ∞. For each i apply 4.4–4.5 to the IM current R_{φ₁(i)} (its boundary has locally finite mass) and the Lipschitz function f := −ψ_c: for a.e. t the slice ⟨R_{φ₁(i)}, f, t⟩ is IM, carried by f⁻¹(t), and equals ∂(R_{φ₁(i)}⌞{f < t}) − (∂R_{φ₁(i)})⌞{f < t}; and ∫ M_{W₀}(⟨R_{φ₁(i)}, f, t⟩) dt ≤ L₀·M_{W₀}(R_{φ₁(i)}). For α ∈ (0, 1) and t = −α, {f < t} = W_α and f⁻¹(t) = Σ_α ⊆ W₀, so P_i(α) := ⟨R_{φ₁(i)}, f, −α⟩ satisfies M(P_i(α)) = M_{W₀}(P_i(α)) and ∫_0^1 Σ_i M(P_i(α)) dα ≤ L₀Σ_i a_{φ₁(i)} < ∞. Choose α ∈ (0, 1) outside the union of the following null sets: the levels where for some i the slice is not IM or the slice identity fails (countably many null sets); the levels with Σ_i M(P_i(α)) = ∞; and the levels with μ_{S_{φ₁(i)}}(Σ_α) > 0 for some i (for each i these are countably many, because the Σ_α are pairwise disjoint subsets of the compact set tsupport ψ_c ⊆ U_{φ₁(i)}, which has finite μ_{S_{φ₁(i)}}-measure). Fix such α, put W := W_α, Σ := Σ_α, F := F_α, O' := B_G ∩ {ψ_c < α} (open), so B_G is the disjoint union of W, Σ and O', and F ⊆ tsupport ψ_c ⊆ ball(0, G/3). Set φ' := φ₁ and re-index: S_i := S_{φ₁(i)}, Ŝ_i, R_i, S'_i, U_i, A_i, π_i accordingly, P_i := P_i(α). Then P_i is IM, spt P_i ⊆ Σ (4.8), M(P_i) → 0, μ_{S_i}(Σ) = 0, and ∂(R_i⌞W) = (∂R_i)⌞W + P_i. With R̃_i := R_i⌞W and S̃_i := S'_i⌞W − P_i (IM by F5, F4), restricting C − Ŝ_i = ∂R_i + S'_i to W gives book (6): C⌞W = Ŝ_i⌞W + ∂R̃_i + S̃_i, and M(S̃_i) ≤ μ_{S'_i}(W) + M(P_i) ≤ a_i + M(P_i) → 0 (book (7)).
6. (The competitor.) Let S be IM with SameBoundary S C and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then X := S − C is IM (G), ∂X = 0, spt X ⊆ K ⊆ W. Y_i := X + ∂R̃_i, where ∂R̃_i = (C − Ŝ_i)⌞W − S̃_i is IM (F4, F5); so Y_i is IM, ∂Y_i = 0, and spt Y_i ⊆ closure W ∪ spt P_i ⊆ F ⊆ ball(0, G/3) is compact. Push-forward (Simon 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9, 2.29): for an IM Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) whose support is a compact subset of ball(0, 2G) and i ≥ j₀, π_{i#}Q(ω) := ∫_{M_Q} θ_Q⟨ω(π_i(y)), Dπ_i(y)_#ξ_Q(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y) defines an IM current (3.9) with spt π_{i#}Q ⊆ π_i(spt Q) (ω ∘ π_i vanishes on spt Q if ω vanishes near π_i(spt Q); F3); it is additive in Q; ∂π_{i#}Q = π_{i#}∂Q if ∂Q has finite mass (2.24(1) for the mollified maps and 2.29), so π_{i#}Y_i is a cycle; and M(π_{i#}Q) ≤ L^n·M(Q) if ‖Dπ_i‖ ≤ L on ball(0, 2G), because |Dπ_i(y)_#(τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ)| ≤ ‖Dπ_i(y)‖ⁿ (Hadamard) and |⟨α, v⟩| ≤ |α||v| for the Euclidean norms. Now spt π_{i#}Y_i ⊆ π_i(F) ⊆ A_i ∩ closedBall(0, 2G/3) ⊆ A_i ∩ B_G (R1). Let Z_i := S_i + π_{i#}Y_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U_i) (π_{i#}Y_i regarded in U_i). Z_i is IM (F4), ∂Z_i = ∂S_i, and spt(Z_i − S_i) is a compact subset of A_i ∩ B_G, while B_G is open with compact closure in U_i (R2). Minimality of S_i in A_i (with the open set B_G) gives M_{B_G}(S_i) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z_i).
7. (π_i fixes S_i near B_G; parent step 4.5.) Let (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i) represent S_i and Q_i := S_i⌞B_G (IM, support ⊆ closedBall(0, G)). Claim: π_{i#}Q_i = Q_i. By F3 and spt S_i ⊆ A_i, Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M_i lies in A_i; let M'_i := M_i ∩ B_G ∩ A_i, so Hⁿ((M_i ∩ B_G) ∖ M'_i) = 0 and π_i(z) = z for z ∈ M'_i (R1). Let y ∈ M'_i be a point (Hⁿ-a.e. point of M_i ∩ B_G) where HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_i y Q_y holds and ξ_i(y) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of Q_y. (a) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M'_i y Q_y: inside any bounded set and for small r, η_{y,r}(M_i) and η_{y,r}(M'_i) differ by the image of an Hⁿ-null set (Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(Z)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(Z)) because y lies in the open B_G. (b) Every unit v ∈ Q_y is a limit of (z_k − y)/|z_k − y| with z_k ∈ M'_i ∖ {y}, z_k → y: otherwise there are ε', r' > 0 such that M'_i ∩ (ball(y, r') ∖ {y}) avoids the cone {z : |(z − y)/|z − y| − v| < ε'}, so for r < r' the set η_{y,r}(M'_i) misses the open set Ω := {w : 1/2 < |w| < 1, |w/|w| − v| < ε'}; testing (a) with f ∈ C_c, 0 ≤ f, supported in Ω and positive at (3/4)v gives 0 → ∫_{Q_y} f dHⁿ > 0, a contradiction. (c) π_i is differentiable at y and π_i(z_k) = z_k, π_i(y) = y, so (I − Dπ_i(y))(z_k − y) = o(|z_k − y|) and hence (I − Dπ_i(y))v = 0. Thus Dπ_i(y) is the identity on Q_y, Dπ_i(y)_#ξ_i(y) = ξ_i(y) and ω(π_i(y)) = ω(y), so π_{i#}Q_i(ω) = ∫_{M_i ∩ B_G} θ_i⟨ω(y), ξ_i(y)⟩ dHⁿ = Q_i(ω). Consequently, for ω supported in B_G, Z_i(ω) = Q_i(ω) + π_{i#}Y_i(ω) = π_{i#}(Q_i + Y_i)(ω), so for i ≥ j(η): M_{B_G}(Z_i) ≤ M(π_{i#}(Q_i + Y_i)) ≤ (1 + η)ⁿM(Q_i + Y_i). Moreover M(Q_i + Y_i) = μ_{Q_i+Y_i}(ℝ^P) = μ_{S_i+Y_i}(B_G): on B_G the IM currents Q_i + Y_i and S_i + Y_i agree (F2), and μ_{Q_i+Y_i}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) ≤ μ_{Q_i}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) + μ_{Y_i}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0 (F4, F3). Hence (I) μ_{S_i}(B_G) = M_{B_G}(S_i) ≤ (1 + η)ⁿ μ_{S_i+Y_i}(B_G) for i ≥ j(η).
8. (Comparison off W; book (8)–(11).) (a) μ_{S_i}(B_G) = μ_{S_i}(W) + μ_{S_i}(Σ) + μ_{S_i}(O') = μ_{S_i}(W) + μ_{S_i}(O'). (b) Y_i vanishes on forms supported in O' (spt Y_i ⊆ F is disjoint from O'; V), so μ_{S_i+Y_i}(O') = μ_{S_i}(O') (F2). (c) μ_{S_i+Y_i}(Σ) ≤ μ_{S_i}(Σ) + μ_{Y_i}(Σ) = μ_{Y_i}(Σ) (F4), and from Y_i = X + (C − Ŝ_i)⌞W − S'_i⌞W + P_i, μ_{Y_i}(Σ) ≤ μ_X(Σ) + μ_{(C−Ŝ_i)⌞W}(Σ) + μ_{S'_i⌞W}(Σ) + μ_{P_i}(Σ) ≤ 0 + 0 + 0 + M(P_i): Σ ∩ K = ∅ (ψ_c = 1 on K, α < 1) and spt X ⊆ K (F3); restrictions to W are carried by W (F5). (d) For ω supported in W ⊆ ball(0, ρ_i): (S_i + Y_i)(ω) = Ŝ_i(ω) + X(ω) + ∂R̃_i(ω) (hypothesis (5)) = C(ω) − S̃_i(ω) + X(ω) (book (6) evaluated at ω) = (S − S̃_i)(ω); so μ_{S_i+Y_i}(W) = μ_{S−S̃_i}(W) ≤ μ_S(W) + M(S̃_i) (F2, F4). (e) By (I) and (a)–(d), for i ≥ j(η): μ_{S_i}(W) + μ_{S_i}(O') ≤ (1 + η)ⁿ[μ_S(W) + M(S̃_i) + M(P_i) + μ_{S_i}(O')]. All terms are finite (μ_{S_i}(O') ≤ μ_{S_i}(B_G) ≤ c_G by (R3); μ_S(W) < ∞ as W is bounded), so μ_{S_i}(W) ≤ μ_S(W) + M(S̃_i) + M(P_i) + ((1 + η)ⁿ − 1)(μ_S(W) + M(S̃_i) + M(P_i) + c_G). (f) Letting i → ∞ (M(S̃_i), M(P_i) → 0): limsup_i μ_{S_i}(W) ≤ μ_S(W) + ((1 + η)ⁿ − 1)(μ_S(W) + c_G) for every η > 0, hence limsup_i μ_{S_i}(W) ≤ μ_S(W). By F1, μ_{S_i}(W) = M_W(S_i) and μ_S(W) = M_W(S).
9. (Output.) W = W_α is open with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K); φ' = φ₁ is strictly increasing and was chosen before S (it depends only on K, ε, ψ and the data); and limsup_i M_W(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_W(S) for every admissible S. Undoing step 1 gives the claim for S_{ψ(φ'(i))}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to ψ = id (hypotheses are stable under subsequences) and fix a cut-off ψ_c with level sets W_s ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and inside B_{G/3}(0).

Flat convergence (Simon 6.7.2) writes C − Ŝ_j = ∂R_j + S'_j with masses on W₀ tending to 0; slicing R_j by ψ_c (Simon 6.4.5) at a good level α along a further subsequence gives C⌞W_α = Ŝ_i⌞W_α + ∂R̃_i + S̃_i with M(S̃_i), M(P_i) → 0 and no S_i-mass on {ψ_c = α}.

For a competitor S, Y_i := (S − C) + ∂R̃_i is a compactly supported IM cycle; Z_i := S_i + π_{i#}Y_i is an admissible competitor in A_i ∩ B_G, and since π_i fixes S_i⌞B_G a.e. with Dπ_i = id on its tangent planes, M_{B_G}(S_i) ≤ (1+η)ⁿμ_{S_i+Y_i}(B_G).
Splitting B_G into W_α, {ψ_c = α} and the rest (book (9)–(11)) yields μ_{S_i}(W_α) ≤ μ_S(W_α) + errors → limsup ≤ M_{W_α}(S).

subproblems.title: Minimality of the limit and convergence of mass measures from the local comparison inequality (Simon 7.2.4 (8), (12)–(14))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity. Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ) and μ_{S_j} → μ_C for all integer multiplicity representations, i.e. MassMeasuresConverge S C: for all IMReps R_j of S_j and R of C and every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dR.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ j, IsOpen (Us j)) → (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S → SameBoundary S C → (S - C).support ⊆ K → limsup (fun j => (Ss (ψ (φ' j))).massOn W) atTop ≤ S.massOn W) → IsMinimizingIn C univ ∧ MassMeasuresConverge Ss C

Source: steps 5 and 6.1–6.4 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon 7.2.4, (8) and its localization, (12)–(14) and the closing approximation argument (chapter-07.txt lines 226–288), including the subsequence-of-subsequence remark of lines 278–280. Siblings used: measure_locality (MEAS), radon_criterion (RADON). Inherited dependencies: dtc_mass_eq_measure (M), dtc_vanish_off_support (V).
0. (Preliminaries.) (L1) For a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any set O, Y.massOn O = Y.massOn (O ∩ V): the admissible forms are test forms in V, whose tsupport lies in V, so the two admissible sets coincide. (L2) If V is open, Y is represented by R_Y and O is open, then Y.massOn O = R_Y.measure O: by L1 and M (O ∩ V is an open subset of V), Y.massOn O = R_Y.measure (O ∩ V) = R_Y.measure O, the carrier lying in V. (L3, lower semicontinuity) For every bounded open O and every strictly increasing φ', C.massOn O ≤ liminf_i (S_{φ'(i)}).massOn O. Indeed, let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n O. closure O ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R, so by (1), for all large j, tsupport ω ⊆ U_j, currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω_j) with ω_j ∈ massAdmissibleOn U_j n O the same form, and ofReal(currentEval(S_j, ω)) ≤ S_j.massOn O. By (2), currentEval(S_{φ'(i)}, ω) → C(ω), so ofReal(C(ω)) = lim_i ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ'(i)}, ω)) ≤ liminf_i S_{φ'(i)}.massOn O; take the supremum over ω.
1. (Minimality of C; book (8) and its localization.) C is integer multiplicity by hypothesis. Let W be open with CompactlyContained W univ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S C, (S − C).support compact and ⊆ univ ∩ W. Put K := (S − C).support, a compact subset of the open set W, and choose ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open). Apply (3) with K, ε and ψ := id: an open W' with K ⊆ W' ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and φ' with limsup_i S_{φ'(i)}.massOn W' ≤ S.massOn W'. W' is bounded, so by L3, C.massOn W' ≤ liminf_i S_{φ'(i)}.massOn W' ≤ limsup_i S_{φ'(i)}.massOn W' ≤ S.massOn W'. Let R_C, R_S represent C, S and μ_C := R_C.measure, μ_S := R_S.measure. The set O := ℝ^P ∖ K is open; if ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and tsupport ω ⊆ O then tsupport ω is disjoint from spt(S − C) = K, so (S − C)(ω) = 0 by V, i.e. currentEval(S, ω) = currentEval(C, ω). MEAS (U₁ = U₂ = ℝ^P, W := O) gives μ_S = μ_C on Borel subsets of O, in particular on W ∖ W' ⊆ O. Using L2: C.massOn W = μ_C(W) = μ_C(W') + μ_C(W ∖ W') = C.massOn W' + μ_S(W ∖ W') ≤ S.massOn W' + μ_S(W ∖ W') = μ_S(W') + μ_S(W ∖ W') = μ_S(W) = S.massOn W. Hence IsMinimizingIn C univ.
2. (Mass measures; book (12)–(14).) Let R_j represent S_j for every j, R represent C, μ_j := R_j.measure, μ := R.measure, and let f be continuous with compact support (tsupport f ⊆ univ is trivial). We verify the hypotheses of RADON.
 (a) For compact K, μ(K) = ∫⁻_{K ∩ carrier} θ_R dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult (K ⊆ univ).
 (c) For bounded open G, μ(G) = C.massOn G ≤ liminf_j S_j.massOn G = liminf_j μ_j(G) (L2, L3 with φ' = id, L2).
 (b) Let K be compact and ε > 0; we show limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) =: a. Otherwise pick b with a < b < limsup_j μ_j(K); then μ_j(K) > b for infinitely many j, so there is a strictly increasing ψ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i (Mathlib Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop). Apply (3) with K, ε, ψ and the competitor S := C, which is admissible: C is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary C C holds, and C − C = 0 has empty support (the zero current vanishes on every ball, which is open with compact closure, so its zero region is ℝ^P; checked in Lean). We get an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and φ' with limsup_i S_{ψ(φ'(i))}.massOn W ≤ C.massOn W = μ(W) ≤ a. But by L2, S_{ψ(φ'(i))}.massOn W = μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(K) > b for every i, so the lim sup is ≥ b > a, a contradiction. Finally K is closed, so the sets thickening(1/q, K) decrease to K, and μ(thickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a) (it lies in a compact set); by continuity from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed) μ(thickening(1/q, K)) → μ(K). Hence limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).
 RADON now gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ. Since the representations and f were arbitrary, MassMeasuresConverge S C holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass on open sets equals the weight of any representation, and mass is lower semicontinuous along currentEval convergence on bounded open sets.
Minimality: the comparison set W' ⊇ spt(S − C) gives M_{W'}(C) ≤ liminf ≤ limsup ≤ M_{W'}(S); since S = C off spt(S − C), measure_locality transfers the inequality to W.
Upper bound on compacts by contradiction: along a bad subsequence the comparison with S = C gives limsup μ_j(K) ≤ μ_C(thickening(ε, K)); let ε ↓ 0.
Lower bound on bounded open sets by lower semicontinuity; radon_criterion yields convergence of ∫ f dμ_j for every representation.
